meanings.note: For emphasis.

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

вообще-то.gloss: actually, as a matter of fact

meanings.en: actually, as a matter of fact, for the record
meanings.note: Polite or pointed correction.

examples.text: Меня вообще-то Юля зовут. Вот сахар.
examples.trans: My name is actually Yulia. Here's the sugar.

meanings.note: In 'до встречи' = until we meet.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + dative of person + accusative of thing
+ infinitive: не даёт мне готовить
imperative давай/давайте + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

related.gloss: to hand in; to take (an exam)

examples.trans: The door is behind the wardrobe.
Open the door. Is this flat nine?
Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: + genitive.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Ещё больше = even more.

examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative.
+ instrumental.
Colloquial insult or exclamation.

examples.trans: Do you take me for an idiot?

examples.text: У вас даже синяка нет. Вы меня за идиота держите?
examples.trans: You don't even have a bruise. Do you take me for an idiot?

examples.text: Боже мой! Какой же я идиот!
examples.trans: My goodness! What an idiot I am!

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: In questions.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!

meanings.note: Hard solid mineral matter.

examples.trans: And he hit his head against a stone.

meanings.note: Unit of weight.

examples.trans: Give me two kilograms of apples, please.

examples.text: Говорят, собака нашла запах плохой травы! Тут пять килограммов сгорело!

meanings.note: кража со взломом = burglary

examples.trans: This is no theft at all.

examples.text: Между прочим, это кража со взломом!

meanings.note: + instrumental; между собой = between yourselves/themselves

examples.text: Ну ладно, вы тут между собой договоритесь.
examples.trans: All right, you two sort it out between yourselves here.

мешать.gloss: to be in the way, to disturb

meanings.en: to be in the way, to hinder
meanings.note: + dative.
Не мешай! = Don't bother me!
cooking: мешать ложкой = to stir with a spoon

examples.trans: The radiators are in the way.

examples.text: Филиппыч, миксер проехать не может. Радиаторы мешают.
examples.trans: Filippych, the mixer truck can't get through. The radiators are in the way.

meanings.note: after numbers: два миллиона, пять миллионов

examples.text: Значит, предложение такое. Ты мне говоришь, где твои сорок миллионов.
examples.trans: So, here's the offer. You tell me where your forty million is.

meanings.note: + genitive plural: много дел.
Comparative.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: + infinitive.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bore, to get on someone's nerves', paired with 'надоедать'.

examples.text: Надоело мне в этом архиве сидеть.
examples.trans: I'm tired of sitting in this archive.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: ночью = at night; спокойной ночи = good night

examples.text: Ну что, Аркаша? Наступила ночь, просыпается мафия.

examples.trans: I've always dreamed of meeting my boyfriend's friends.

meanings.note: + dative: 'позвони мне' = call me. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'звонить').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Right, the operation goes on. Mikhail Mikhailovich, give Lavrov your help.

meanings.en: to clean; to peel (vegetables); to brush (teeth)
meanings.note: почистить картошку = to peel potatoes

examples.text: Герман попросил до вечера почистить два мешка картошки.
examples.trans: Herman asked us to peel two sacks of potatoes by evening.

examples.text: Всю морковку почистили, ещё дудку сделали.
examples.trans: They peeled all the carrots and even made a pipe.

meanings.note: from a trip, by car, train or plane

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, there's a child here, we're having breakfast. And the television, by the way, is ours!

meanings.note: + 3rd person verb: 'пусть строят' = let them build

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: the noun after it is genitive plural: пятьдесят метров

examples.text: Пятьдесят метров, не больше. Иначе будет сигнал.
examples.trans: Fifty metres, no more. Otherwise there'll be a signal.

meanings.note: + infinitive: решил стать = decided to become
Решить задачу.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: instrumental of утро used as an adverb

час.governs: after 2, 3, 4 and полтора the genitive часа is stressed on the ending

В два часа = at two o'clock. Common masculine noun meaning 'hour' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in an hour.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: Informal. Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.
